svg.title: Victoria rabbit trapping and food decision gate
svg.desc: A working two-panel decision card. Panel A says not to make or set an improvised snare, deadfall or leg-hold trap in Victoria and summarises the permission boundary for compliant rabbit leg-hold and confinement traps. Panel B requires positive rabbit identity, lawful permission, a compliant familiar trap, regular inspection and non-target care, humane dispatch competence, positively known site baiting and poison-treatment history, disease checks, hygienic processing and no loss of higher survival priorities. Any no or unknown answer means do not trap or eat. The card includes farmed-rabbit food-composition values only as a comparison and gives no trap construction, bait, placement, dispatch, cutting or cooking method.
svg.text: RABBIT FOOD — NO SNARE SHORTCUT
WORKING CARD · PANEL A OF 2 · VICTORIA
STOP — DO NOT IMPROVISE A SNARE OR DEADFALL
Non-kill snares and kill traps require prior Victorian approval.
A rabbit leg-hold or cage trap still needs lawful equipment, permission,
checking, non-target care and humane dispatch. Hunger is not a blanket exception.
CONFIDENCE + LIMIT
High evidence confidence for trap categories; Moderate for this short legal summary.
94% wording estimate only — not legal advice, food safety or survival odds.
IMPROVISED WIRE / CORD SNARE OR DEADFALL
DO NOT MAKE OR SET ONE. No bait or placement method is supplied.
COMPLIANT SMALL LEG-HOLD TRAP
Rabbits only · private land with owner/occupier approval · never possess or
use on Crown land · urban use also needs Ministerial approval.
COMPLIANT CONFINEMENT / CAGE TRAP
Prior land consent · minimise injury and non-target capture · inspect as often as possible.
The legal maximum is not a target · humane killing as soon as reasonably possible.
PRE-PLANNED SYSTEMS ONLY · READ PANEL B · NEVER USE THIS PANEL DETACHED
CAPTURE IS NOT YET FOOD
WORKING CARD · PANEL B OF 2 · PANEL A CONTROLS
EVERY CHECK MUST BE YES BEFORE A TRAP IS SET
One NO or UNKNOWN = DO NOT TRAP. Keep rescue, warmth, shelter and water first.
□ Positive European-rabbit identity — not hare, native animal or pet
□ Exact method lawful here today; required permission or approval held
□ Purpose-made compliant trap; already trained to use and inspect it
□ Safe plan for weather, non-target capture and an injured animal
□ Reviewed humane-dispatch skill and suitable equipment
□ Site baiting and poison-treatment history positively known — unknown = STOP
□ Live capture; no abnormal behaviour, disease sign or chemical concern
□ Hygienic dressing, cooling and cooking can be completed safely
This card supplies none of the missing capture, dispatch or processing methods.
FOOD VALUE — COMPARISON ONLY
Farmed rabbit, raw meat: 472 kJ / about 113 kcal per 100 g.
Casseroled rabbit flesh, no added fat: 712 kJ / about 170 kcal per 100 g.
FSANZ records F007601 and F007602. Not wild-rabbit values or carcass yield.
Do not budget calories until matching edible cooked flesh is weighed.
SIGNS ARE NOT PERMISSION OR PLACEMENT
Warrens, dung or grazing marks do not clear species, land, trap or food.
NO CONSTRUCTION · NO PLACEMENT · NO DISPATCH · NOT FIELD-APPROVED
